The raw_merchants table has 46 rows for 40 distinct merchant_ids. Six ids appear twice, and the copies are identical in every column. The join in gold_mcc_daily therefore fans out and inflates the count. The extra rows account for the gap: 5416 − 4699 = 717 rows, which fits transactions for those six merchants being counted twice.

The fix is to deduplicate in silver_merchants. Because the copies are fully identical, SELECT DISTINCT is safe. To be robust, I group by merchant_id and take any(mcc). That is equivalent here, since the copies do not differ.

The other gold tables do not depend on merchants. gold_merchant_daily reads silver_transactions directly, so it is unaffected.
